prompt:
We're doing an attestation review for our `payment-router` skill (v3.1) before it goes to production. We're using three validators — Validator-A (PayAudit Inc), Validator-B (SecureCheck Ltd), and Validator-C (TrustLab Systems) — and our compliance board wants to know if these three validators are really giving us three independent opinions, or if some of them are essentially duplicating the same check.

We have the validators' disclosed metadata in the `validators/` directory, 50 edge-case attestation verdicts in `attestation/results/edge_case_verdicts.csv`, evasion probe results in `attestation/edge_cases/evasion_transferability.json`, and reasoning traces from all three validators in the `traces/` directory. Note that one validator has not disclosed its training provenance, so we'll need to rely on its published reasoning traces to assess independence.

Please produce a comprehensive correlation analysis report saved as `correlation_report.txt`. The compliance board specifically wants to know: which validators (if any) are epistemically correlated, what the effective number of truly independent validators is, and what detection approach was used.
